triggers.name: An issue was opened or changed
triggers.description: Tells you when an issue in one repository is opened, edited, labelled, commented on, closed or reopened. It polls until Fabric is hosted. Pull requests are a separate trigger. A deleted issue is not reported. A change that lands during a long catch-up can skip one item.

triggers.name: A comment was added or edited
triggers.description: Tells you when a comment on an issue or pull request conversation in one repository is added or edited. Review comments on a diff and commit comments are not included. A deleted comment is not reported. It polls until Fabric is hosted. A change that lands during a long catch-up can skip one item.

triggers.name: A pull request was opened or changed
triggers.description: Tells you when a pull request in one repository is opened, edited, reviewed, commented on, closed or merged. It reads the same list as the issue trigger, so one request serves both. It polls until Fabric is hosted. A change that lands during a long catch-up can skip one item.

triggers.name: A branch moved
triggers.description: Tells you when a branch in one repository is pushed to, force pushed, created, deleted or merged into, one event for each change GitHub lists in the repository activity. Tags are not promised. It polls until Fabric is hosted.

triggers.name: A workflow run finished
triggers.description: Tells you when a GitHub Actions run in one repository finishes, one event for each attempt, with how it ended. Queued and running states are not reported. GitHub lists runs by when they started, so a run or a re-run that finishes behind the 100 newest can be missed. Fabric says so only when it finds a finished run at the end of what it reads. It polls until Fabric is hosted. A change that lands during a long catch-up can skip one item.

triggers.name: A GitHub notification arrived
triggers.description: Tells you when a thread in your GitHub notifications is new or has news, in any repository you get notifications for. It always polls: GitHub has no webhook for notifications. It waits at least as long as GitHub says between polls. A change that lands during a long catch-up can skip one item.

triggers.name: A release was published
triggers.description: Tells you when a release in one repository is published, once for each release. Drafts and later edits are not reported, and a tag with no release is not one. GitHub lists releases by commit date, so a release on a commit older than the 90 newest can be missed. Fabric says so only when it finds a new release at the end of what it reads. It polls until Fabric is hosted. A change that lands during a long catch-up can skip one item.
